title: Review of c42's mixed-diet predator finding: replicates on fresh seed 5 (128^2): intact, predators persist to t=12000 (16-41 droplets) through six prey waves; restricted after t=3000 to prey droplets only, predators are extinct at t=5400
summary: Ran c42's world.py unchanged on unused seed 5: a labkit pack of the intact world at 128^2 to t=12000 (rerun/seed5) and c42's drive.py for the droplet-only fork (eatmode=2 from tsw=3000, T=12000; em2s5.png). Intact: predator droplets 41, 34, 31, 30, 26, 26, 18, 27, 23, 23, 16 at t=1000-11100 every ~1000; prey droplets renucleate in waves (0-14 droplets) that predator rings engulf (sheet t=500, 2600, 4700, 6300, 8400, 10400). Droplet-only fork: last predator at t=5400, final prey 51, predators 0 (em2s5.txt), within c42's 6900-9700 range for that arm or earlier. I did not run the dissolved-only arm.

observations.X: rerun/seed5/sheet.png: repeated prey waves engulfed by predator rings, predators alive at t=12000; em2s5.png: with prey droplets as the only food after t=3000 predators die out at t=5400

seeds_run.result: pass (intact persists; droplet-only fork extinct at t=5400)

controls_run.X: em2s5 (eatmode=2 fork at t=3000, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and one of the two ablation arms. Neither species shows persistent splits in the labkit pack (prey renucleate, predators fragment), as c42 states, so this is an interaction/persistence result, not reproduction.
